classification.explicit: Rack-squat technique, 3–5 per side and fixed-rep/add-set method in #305; later double-club order/grip/swing-clean teaching in #206.
classification.app: Rack-squat 2–4-set endpoint, 90-second rest, recent goblet evidence, explicit confirmation and complex component gates. Double clubs remain education-only.

instruction.purpose: Train the squat while holding one bell in a stable single-side rack; this is distinct from the two-hand goblet squat.
setup: Use two hands initially to establish the rack. Place the corner of the handle in the hand with the handle angled about 45 degrees.
Keep the wrist straight, elbow close to the hip and thumb near collarbone height. Point feet generally forward.
steps: Descend under control with the rack elbow tracking inside the knee. Use the free hand for initial stabilization if needed.
Keep the chest and trunk controlled; choose an individual comfortable range instead of forcing the source demonstration’s deepest position.
Stand fully, engage quadriceps and glutes, and keep the ribcage controlled. Match repetitions on both sides.
Use the free hand to support the bell and set it down with control.
bracing: Choose repetitions and load that maintain structure and breathing. The transcript does not establish one mandatory breath cadence.
mistakes: Bent wrist or flared elbow: rebuild the rack before adding squat depth.
Treating the source’s deepest squat demonstration as compulsory: preserve comfortable range and control.
Increasing repetitions instead of sets changes intensity in this source’s fixed-weight volume example.

doubleClubReference.name: Double-club swing clean to order
doubleClubReference.purpose: Develop the bottom portion of a double-club swipe: coordinated hip-driven swings into a stable double order.
setup: Double-club work comes later than familiar single-arm and two-hand club work in this lesson. Use familiar manageable clubs with clear space outside the body.
Begin about 12–18 inches behind the clubs, feet generally forward. Reach down with thumbs pointing down, then rotate thumbs up and pack the shoulders.
steps: Hinge into the skiing-like bottom position. Let the clubs swing outside the body while the hips drive the movement.
Pull elbows inward and stop in a controlled double order, rather than a kettlebell rack.
Push, swing, pull and stop deliberately. At the bottom, keep straight arms in line with the body rather than reaching far behind it.
Set the clubs down with the same controlled technique used to pick them up.
bracing: The source describes lat engagement connecting shoulders to the back. It does not prescribe an exact breathing cadence.
The swing uses the traction-style ice-cream-cone grip; the stop compresses the upper hand with the finger/thumb OK grip.
mistakes: Wide elbows or elbows tracking behind the body: rebuild a stable, controlled order.
Treating the catch as a double kettlebell rack: review the different grip and order position.
Turning this coordination practice into a high-volume test: the source’s historical instructor test is context, not a prescription.
qualifications: The source describes this as back-burner coordinated skill practice after familiar swing, snatch or club work, with a couple of sets as an example. No automatic dose is implemented.
Swing clean precedes double pullovers and their later combination into swipes. These educational connections are not automatically measured technical qualifications.
